data.short_meaning: My delight is in the Lord
data.long_meaning: Hephziba is a Hebrew name meaning 'my delight is in the Lord.' It appears in the Bible in 2 Samuel 17:25, as the name of a city in the territory of the Gileadites that was founded by Hushai the Archite when he was helping Absalom, David's son, during a rebellion against David. It can also be interpreted as 'beautiful branch' in Hebrew.
data.spiritual_meaning: Hephziba represents the deep joy and contentment that comes from putting one's trust and faith in the Lord.
data.etymology: Hephziba belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My delight is in the Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hephziba total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: הפציבה
in_hebrew.meaning: הפציבה - שמה של אישה יפהפייה וראויה לאהבה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הפציבה הוא שם עברי שמקורו בתנ"ך, בספר ישעיהו. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'הפ' ו'ציבה'. 'הפ' היא חלקיק שמשמעותו 'ה' או 'היא', ו'ציבה' פירושו 'שלו' או 'אהובה'. לכן, הפציבה פירושו 'היא תהיה לי שמחה' או 'היא תהיה אהובה שלי'. השם הפציבה מוזכר בספר ישעיהו, פרק לז, פסוק 26, כשמה של אזור בארץ ישראל.

in_greek.name: Ἠφζίβα
in_greek.meaning: Ἠφζίβα - ὄνομα γυναικός, ἡ ἀγάπη και χαρά
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἠφζίβα (Ēphziba) εἰς τὸ Ἑβραϊκὸν ὄνομα, ῾Ηפציבה (Hephtzibah), ὃ σημαίνει 'ἡ ἀγάπη καὶ χαρά μου' ἤ 'ἡ ἐπιθυμία μου'. Ἠφζίβα εἰς τὴν Καινή Διαθήκη οὐκ ἀναφέρεται ἀλλὰ εἰς τὴν Ἑβραϊκὴν Βίβλον, εἰς τὸ βιβλίον Ἠσαΐα, κεφάλαιο 37, εὐαγγέλιον 26.

historical_references.reference: Hephzibah, a city in the Old Testament, is mentioned in the book of Isaiah (4:5-6) as a symbol of God's comfort and joy. It is prophesied that the Lord will extend peace to her, and she will be called the 'rest' and 'refuge' of the Lord. The name Hephzibah is interpreted as 'my delight is in her', indicating the deep affection God has for his people.

Hephzibah, a daughter of King Solomon, is mentioned in the New Testament (1 Kings 4:21) as one of the wives of Eliahah, a son of King Jehoiakim. She is also known as the mother of King Zedekiah, the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile. The name Hephzibah means 'my delight is in her', reflecting the affection King Solomon had for her.
